items.markdown:
If you’re looking around **Newcastle-under-Lyme**, I’d be cautious about choosing a puppy simply because an advert says “blue Staffy.” The blue/grey coat is a colour, not an indicator of health or breeding quality, and you should prioritise the parents’ health testing, temperament and the breeder’s practices.

### Places to start

- The Staffordshire Bull Terrier Club — based in Cannock. A breed club is a useful place to ask about reputable local breeders and upcoming litters.
- City Dogs Home — in Stoke-on-Trent. If you're open to adoption rather than specifically buying a puppy, it's worth checking whether Staffies or Staffy crosses are available.
- I found several businesses advertising Staffies further afield, but I **wouldn't treat the search listing itself as evidence that they're reputable breeders**. I'd verify them independently before making contact.

The [thekennelclub.org.uk](https://www.thekennelclub.org.uk/search/find-a-puppy/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) is another good starting point. The Kennel Club's Staffordshire Bull Terrier guidance and breed-specific health recommendations should also be part of your checks. [The Kennel Club](https://www.thekennelclub.org.uk/media/2703/22-may-2019-minutes.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com) [The Kennel Club](https://www.thekennelclub.org.uk/media/1086/22-may-2019-agenda.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com) 

### What to ask the breeder

I'd ask these before paying a deposit:

1. **“Can I see the mother with the puppies?”**
 Ideally see the puppies where they were raised. Be wary if you're offered a meeting somewhere else or aren't allowed to see the mother.
2. **“What health tests have both parents had, and can I see the certificates?”**
 Don't accept just “they're healthy.” Ask for the actual results. For Staffies, ask specifically about the breed-relevant DNA tests and other recommended screening.
3. **“Can I see the parents' Kennel Club registration details?”**
 Registration alone doesn't guarantee a healthy puppy, but it allows you to investigate the pedigree and recorded information.
4. **“Why did you choose this mating?”**
 A good breeder should be able to explain the reasoning in terms of health, temperament and conformation—not simply “because they're blue.”
5. **“How old are the puppies and when can they leave?”**
 Don't take a puppy away prematurely.
6. **“What vaccinations, microchipping, worming and veterinary checks have been done?”**
 Ask for paperwork rather than relying on verbal assurances.
7. **“What happens if I can't keep the dog later?”**
 A responsible breeder should be interested in the dog's lifetime welfare and normally have a policy for taking a dog back or helping rehome it.
8. **“Can I meet previous owners of your puppies?”**
 Genuine references can be useful, although you should still do your own checks.
9. **“Are there any health or temperament problems in the parents, grandparents or previous litters?”**
 Ask this directly and see whether the answer is detailed and transparent.
10. **“Can I have the contract before I pay a deposit?”**
 Read the terms carefully, including health guarantees, registration, return arrangements and what happens if veterinary problems are discovered.

### One particular warning about “blue Staffies”

I'd be especially wary of adverts that heavily emphasise **“rare blue,” “blue and tan,” “exclusive colour,”** etc. A breeder charging a premium because a puppy is blue isn't necessarily doing anything wrong, but colour shouldn't be the main selling point. I'd be much more interested in **documented health testing and the temperament and health history of the whole breeding line**.

If you want, I can also **search specifically for current Staffordshire Bull Terrier litters within, say, 50 miles of Newcastle-under-Lyme and separate the potentially reputable breeders from the adverts I'd approach cautiously.**
